# Anivora 0.1.27 — Reader, comments and expanded avatars

- Manga reader chapter buttons now skip to the previous/next chapter from any page and start at page one. Page swipes and the scrubber move within a chapter. Rapid taps cannot skip multiple chapters accidentally.
- Left-to-right, right-to-left and vertical reading preserve the current page when switching modes. RTL mirrors the scrubber. Fit Width, Fit Height, Original Size, background colors and page-number preferences persist. Chapter navigation also supports downloaded chapters and saved reading progress.
- Comments use larger filter buttons and composer controls, following the Th3-Anime reference. Previously loaded public comments are saved on the device and remain readable during API outages. Comments not previously loaded still need the server.
- Every Send attempt rechecks the API. While unavailable, the existing server notice appears again, the draft stays intact, and no comment is submitted. Sending resumes after recovery. Existing app-entry outage/recovery notices and other announcements remain available.
- Added 72 bundled character portraits, bringing the picker to 146 choices across 32 anime groups. All 74 existing choices and identifiers remain available. New groups include Frieren, Solo Leveling, Black Clover, Blue Lock, Code Geass, Dr. Stone, Mob Psycho 100 and Noragami.

Android version code: **29**. Package: `com.brandon300.anivora`. ARM64, Android 7.0/API 24 or newer, signed with the existing certificate for installation over the previous app. APK downloads continue through the public GitHub release feed. The publisher now verifies the complete unauthenticated APK download before advancing latest.json.

Validation: TypeScript, lint, 219 app tests, backend tests, Expo compatibility checks and browser touch/interaction checks for reader modes, chapter jumps, offline comments and avatar selection. APK signature, package/version, architecture, ZIP alignment and compiled-source identity are checked before publication. Physical installation and exact native rendering on an Infinix Hot 50i require a device check; browser checks do not certify native pixels.

Source commit: https://github.com/brandon-300/Anivora/commit/a2efdb0e7836c5a92cca91d0069dc55f7f7099f9

Build validation: local Gradle release build succeeded; TypeScript, lint, 219 app tests, 47 backend tests, Expo Doctor 18/18 and all 48 native unit tests passed. Package, existing signing certificate, ARM64 architecture, ZIP alignment, compiled source/bundle identity (73 source files) and all 77 bundled avatar image resources were verified. Browser interaction checks passed for reader controls, offline comments and profile avatars.

GitHub Actions attempt: https://github.com/brandon-300/Anivora/actions/runs/40482728652 — FFmpeg package installation through the runner's Azure mirror timed out after ten minutes; Android emulator integration did not run for this release. This commit corrects the mirror in both legacy and deb822 APT source files. The signed APK was built and verified locally, then published through the existing public GitHub publisher. Physical Infinix Hot 50i installation/rendering remains unverified.

Publication uses the existing GitHub Actions public publisher after rechecking the signed local APK, source/bundle hashes, archive checksum and native test evidence. Six additional transport validation tests cover corrupted archives, missing metadata, unsafe filenames and source mismatches.
